investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the VM readiness or lifecycle assertions required by the expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, indicating the peer-pod VM slot quota on those nodes was fully consumed at the time of the eval run. The other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector rules, making them ineligible regardless of resource availability. Preemption was also exhausted: no lower-priority victims were found on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for 148 seconds before the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence object and failing all contract assertions. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place new pods: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both report insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes. Every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was rejected by the scheduler with "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" on those 2 nodes and "node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" on the other 4. Preemption was also unavailable ("No preemption victims found"). Because no pod could be scheduled, the agent lifecycle never progressed past creation, the state-polling probe had no agent to query, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) remained absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the VM readiness or lifecycle assertions required by the expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, indicating the peer-pod VM slot quota on those nodes was fully consumed at the time of the eval run. The other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector rules, making them ineligible regardless of resource availability. Preemption was also exhausted: no lower-priority victims were found on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for 148 seconds before the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence object and failing all contract assertions. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in sequence on 2026-06-29 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors reporting zero available nodes due to exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and node affinity mismatches. Because the pod could never be scheduled, no agent was created, and the runtime eval produced zero evidence — every required field (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) is missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity to schedule new peer-pod VMs. Of the 6 nodes in the cluster, only 2 are eligible for kata peer-pod workloads, and both report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" — meaning the VM slot resource on those nodes is fully consumed. The remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector requirements and are therefore ineligible. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. This scheduling blockage prevented agent pod creation for all three remote-agent checks, causing each to time out unscheduled (~141–148 s) and return no evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) as the first substantive step; a scheduling failure here would prevent all downstream evidence collection.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 peer-pod-eligible nodes: existing remote agent pods are consuming all available VM slots, leaving none for new eval-provisioned agents. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity rules, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the impact of any VM slot shortage (evidence: failed-check.message — '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector').

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total cluster size (6 nodes, 2 peer-pod-eligible) may be insufficient for concurrent eval runs plus live workloads, causing contention during the eval window.

Lower probability — a stuck or leaked agent pod from a prior eval run that was not cleaned up, holding VM slots and preventing new scheduling. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs is intended to prevent this, but a prior crash or timeout could leave orphaned pods (evidence: source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1916).

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are available and not exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes, the scheduling failure has a different cause (e.g., a quota, admission webhook, or policy block).

If the 4 non-eligible nodes are found to have been recently reconfigured to accept peer-pod workloads and the affinity rules were not updated, the root cause would shift to a node affinity misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion.

If a subsequent eval run with no concurrent workloads also fails with the same message, it would suggest the 2 eligible nodes have zero kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity configured (provisioning gap) rather than runtime exhaustion.

If the eval passes immediately after the current run without any operator intervention, it would suggest a transient slot-hold by a prior eval pod that self-cleaned, not a sustained capacity shortage.

If only remote-agent-runtime fails while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state pass in a subsequent run, the shared scheduling dependency hypothesis would be weakened and a check-specific issue should be investigated.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity across all peer-pod-eligible nodes before attempting remote agent creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct 'warn' status rather than a scheduling timeout.
Add an eval that detects orphaned remote-agent pods (pods in non-Running, non-Succeeded states older than a configurable threshold) and alerts before they exhaust VM slots.

Add a cluster-health eval that verifies at least N kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are free on peer-pod-eligible nodes, running on a shorter interval than the remote-agent creation evals so capacity warnings precede scheduling failures.

Consider a sibling-correlation eval rule: if all checks under a feature fail with structurally identical scheduler messages within a short time window, auto-classify as a shared infrastructure dependency failure to reduce duplicate investigation overhead.
